answer.rationale: Timing is the strongest signal available: the release landed 2h ago and write-path p99 began climbing 90m ago, which is the ordering you would expect if the build introduced the regression. That makes rollback_release the highest-prior candidate, and memory_b1 is the inherited precedent I am leaning on, so it is the first thing I want the archive to confirm — specifically whether that March-era rollback happened under heavy write load or during a quiet window, because 'finished without customer impact' means very different things in those two cases. I also want memory_b5, because it is the only inherited record that claims a direct write-latency recovery, and it is the main competing explanation: if the current climb is read-amplification or contention from settlement peak rather than the release, routing reads off the primary would be the better single move. Those two verifications discriminate between the two live hypotheses; the others do not. Failover (memory_b2) is explicitly a latency-restoration precedent, not a write-integrity one, and shifting regions mid-settlement-peak risks exactly the in-flight writes the objective protects. add_capacity (memory_b3) was pre-provisioned ahead of a known peak, not applied during an active 90-minute degradation, so it is a slow lever misapplied here. Circuit breakers (memory_b4) contained an external partner failure; there is no partner-outage signal, and failing fast on the write path sheds customer writes, which is the one outcome ruled out. Caveats I am holding rather than resolving: these memories are consolidated summaries, and consolidation strips the conditions that made each action safe — load level, whether the rollback was schema-compatible, whether writes were draining. Correlation in time is not causation; the release and the settlement peak coincide, and a peak-triggered regression that the release merely exposed would not be fixed by reverting. So I intend a small_guarded_test: revert on one cell or a limited cohort, per the staged-gating pattern in memory_b6 that surfaced regressions inside an hour, and read the p99 delta on that cell against the unreverted ones before committing broadly. The material downstream risk I am flagging is that a rollback during peak settlement writes can drop or orphan in-flight transactions if the prior build is not forward-compatible with data written in the last two hours; a guarded partial revert bounds that exposure to one cell instead of the whole write path, and if the archive shows memory_b1's rollback was low-load or schema-neutral, I will treat it as weak support and pivot toward memory_b5's read-offload, which is reversible and touches no write semantics.
